transcript:
[00:00] Ben Carter (Redwood AE): Okay, hey everybody, thanks for joining. Um, I see folks from AuroraCloud - Liam, Sara, Priya, Tom - thanks for making time. Quick agenda: marketplace listing flows, RA (reference architecture) diagram review, perf tests, and security questions. Maya will run through the technical bits.
[00:22] Liam O'Connor (AuroraCloud PM): Thanks Ben. We'll want to get the listing ready for Q4 push, and make sure the joint solution page has the network and security footprint.
[00:30] Maya Singh (Redwood SE): Hi all. I'll share my screen in a sec - but high level, Redwood's marketplace integration needs: listing metadata (SKU, entitlements), connector for billing reconciliation, and either a hosted SaaS or a private listing (VPC/private deployment) option.
[00:48] Sara Lopez (AuroraCloud Eng): When you say "private listing" do you mean our customers would deploy Redwood Private inside their VPC or you run a dedicated instance in Aurora's marketplace infra? Just to clarify terminology.
[01:02] Ben Carter: Good q - we have a couple of patterns. 1) Marketplace just sells a SaaS contract - customers get Redwood hosted API with entitlement from Aurora billing. 2) Marketplace offers a private deployment AMI/container - that's the private/VPC pattern where Redwood ships an image or k8s helm and Aurora handles provisioning. 3) Dedicated model - reserved capacity hosted by Redwood but billed through marketplace.
[01:26] Tom Reed (AuroraCloud): For ease of go-to-market, ops prefers the SaaS entitlements path initially, but we need the RA to show how we handle networking and keys so enterprise buyers are comfortable.
[01:36] Maya: Right, and enterprise customers will ask about KMS integration, SOC2 logs, RBAC, and audit trails. We should show both TLS + customer KMS for encryption at rest when using Private, and also how we can integrate with Aurora's billing tokens for the hosted path.
[01:52] Priya Patel (AuroraCloud Security): On KMS: our customers demand that the key material be customer-controlled. Can Redwood support bring-your-own-KMS or HSM? Also SSO - SAML/SCIM for user sync is required.
[02:06] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS via KMS integration and we have HSM-compatible flows; I'll share the integration doc. There might be some edge cases with on-prem HSMs and certain cipher suites - we'll note those in the RA.
[02:21] Ben: Also to note, for Dedicated pools we can do tenant isolation and dedicated GPU pools; cost/latency tradeoffs show up there. Diego will talk about perf expectations.
[02:33] Diego Ramos (Redwood SA): Quick perf note: For typical chat workloads, dedicated (pinned GPUs) lowers 95th pct latency by ~20-40% depending on batch config. But cost per token is higher unless you have steady throughput. We'll capture numbers in the perf doc.
[02:51] Sara: Can you quantify - like, for a 2k concurrent sessions workload what infra footprint are we looking at?
[02:58] Diego: Roughly, depends on model and quantization - but ballpark, 4 A100-class for a small fleet to maintain interactive latencies; with kv cache and batching we can manage throughput. We can run a benchmark with your sample workload.
[03:12] Liam: That leads to marketplace listing - we need SKU mapping: how customers select hosted vs dedicated vs private during purchase, and what entitlements get provisioned downstream.
[03:24] Ben: Correct. Our proposal: Marketplace listing has three SKUs or a single SKU with tiered entitlements - we'll sync on metadata. Tom, can you share Aurora's listing JSON sample?
[03:33] Tom: Yep, I can export a sample listing. We'll include pricing fields, entitlements, and marketplace tag taxonomy.
[03:40] [00:04:05] Maya: On networking/RA - here's a rough diagram, note the vpc peering / transit gateway option for private deployments; for hosted we use a secure egress and allowlist of control-plane IPs.
[03:56] Sara: Do you support cross-account roles or just API keys?
[04:00] Maya: We support both. For private we prefer cross-account roles with least privilege; for hosted we can issue customer-specific API keys tied to the marketplace entitlement.
[04:12] Priya: Audit logs - we need log forwarding to customer's SIEM or at least retention for 365 days for compliance. Is that configurable?
[04:21] Diego: Yes, audit log retention is configurable in Redwood Console and we support forwarding via syslog or cloud-native log sinks. There are some retention cost implications; we'll highlight that in the RA.
[04:33] [00:04:40] Liam: On testing - we want a small benchmark comparing Redwood Hosted via Marketplace vs Redwood Dedicated in your infra. Could you provide the test harness?
[04:46] Maya: Absolutely. We'll provide a JMeter-like harness and scripts to simulate the chat prompt distribution you described in the pre-meeting notes. We'll also provide guidance for sequence length and concurrency settings.
[04:58] Tom: For marketplace ops, we have to validate the billing reconciliation. How does Redwood surface usage metrics for Aurora to pull?
[05:07] Ben: We can offer a billing export endpoint or SFTP of usage reports with token-level breakdowns. For marketplace reconciliation we typically provide a daily usage CSV or API.
[05:18] Tom: Okay, and that CSV must contain sku_id, customer_id, usage_units, timestamp - we'll validate formats.
[05:26] [00:05:30] Priya: One more on security: pen test requirements - Aurora requires a third-party pen test report or we can do joint assessments. Redwood ok with providing scope?
[05:36] Ben: Yes, we can share pen test summaries and coordinate scope. For Private deployments customers often run their own tests; we can support.
[05:45] Sara: Small nit - when you say "KV cache" in docs, some of our infra folks confuse it with Redis caching; can we clarify that it's model KV cache (attention cache) not general-purpose cache?
[05:58] Diego: Good call - we'll update the RA text to be explicit: KV cache = model key-value attention cache used to accelerate token generation.
[06:08] [00:06:20] Liam: Timeline - we want marketplace listing ready for staging by mid-Oct. Is that feasible?
[06:15] Ben: Yes, with the RA and metadata exchanged this month and the perf tests scheduled for late Sep, we can aim for a staging listing in October.
[06:24] Maya: Action items recap: we'll send the RA draft and perf plan; Aurora to provide listing JSON and KMS requirements.
[06:31] Tom: We'll also put you in touch with our marketplace billing engineer to validate the CSV schema.
[06:36] Priya: One quick question on SSO - scoping for SCIM is required for provisioning. Do you support SCIM v2?
[06:43] Maya: Yes, we support SCIM v2 for user provisioning and SAML for SSO. We'll include the endpoints in the security appendix.
[06:50] [00:07:10] Ben: There's some slight verbal, um, transcriptions might mix up "Aurora" and "Auroracloud" in notes but we'll standardize.
[06:58] Sara: On quantization - do you have recommended model configs for edge vs cloud?
[07:04] Diego: We recommend int8 or bfloat16 quant for cost saving with minor quality tradeoffs; we'll include model/quality guidance per workload in the RA.
[07:15] Liam: Any legal or procurement blockers from Redwood side? We have a standard marketplace contract and need to know if Redwood accepts marketplace revenue share terms or prefers invoicing.
[07:26] Ben: We can be flexible; typical is revenue share for marketplace SaaS, and invoiced reserved contracts for Dedicated. Legal can follow up; I'll loop them in.
[07:36] [00:07:40] Maya: Ok wrapping up - to be specific on deliverables: Redwood sends RA draft + perf plan + security appendix by 2026-09-16; Redwood SE prepares bench scripts by 2026-09-20; Aurora sends listing JSON + KMS requirements by 2026-09-18. We'll schedule benchmark window week of 2026-09-21.
[07:56] Liam: Sounds good. One more ask: can Redwood provide a short "how it works" deck for the marketplace page - 2 slides showing deployment options?
[08:05] Ben: Yep, we can do a 2-slide explainer and a one-page RA summary.
[08:11] [00:08:30] Tom: I'll coordinate with marketplace ops on the SKU taxonomy and send the sample listing JSON after this call.
[08:18] Priya: We'll collect compliance questions and send them to Ben and Maya - mainly KMS key ownership, audit log retention, and data residency.
[08:25] Ben: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links in an email and the drive folder.
[08:31] Maya: Thanks all.
[08:34] [00:08:54] End of recording.
